messages:
maya: Heads-up —I've opened a short proposal for changing admission control to a hybrid model (short queues + graceful degrade + targeted rejects) to reduce long tail latency and avoid head-of-line blocking. RFC: <https://go/internal/rfc/hybrid-admission>. TL;DR: prefer soft degradation over long queues, but allow fast rejects for low-priority traffic. Looking for ops/infra feedback on thresholds and fairness rules.

ram: Sketch looks reasonable. Quick Q — what metrics/triggers do we use to transition between queue -> degrade -> reject? GPU util? queue latency? both?

maya: Plan is: sustained GPU util > 85% for 30s OR p99 queue > 800ms => start soft-degrade. Soft-degrade = reduce max_tokens by X%, switch to smaller model family (if available), and prefer sampling params that reduce cost. If condition continues (e.g., 90%+ or p99 queue > 2s) escalate to probabilistic rejects for low-priority buckets. Open to values.

callie: :thinking_face: How do we avoid big customers starving small ones when we do weighted token budgets? We need something simple to reason about.

maya: We add a weighted-token scheduler: each customer gets a token budget per window; weight = commit_level * priority_factor; when overloaded we scale weights down uniformly but cap max tokens per-request. Heavier customers lose absolute throughput but fairness preserved. Also allow emergency caps for noisy tenants.

liam: Concern: degrading outputs may cause product regressions (bad hallucinations / failure modes). We need an opt-out for high-SLA customers or an explicit comms plan.

maya: Agreed — enterprise tenants can opt out of degrade but must be on Dedicated/reserved capacity or accept higher price. We'll route "no-degrade" tenants to reserved pools when possible.

ram: On queueing architecture: prefer per-worker short micro-queues (<=100ms target) to avoid head-of-line. Global admission layer decides per-request action. Remember autoscale lag ~3m in worst case — we can't rely on it to absorb bursts.

ops-bot: incident-bot: auto-scale event in eu-west-1 at 03:20 UTC — GPU queue length spike x4, request drop observed in low-priority bucket.

callie: Proposal iteration: 1) Degrade after 500-800ms of queueing, 2) fast-reject low-priority requests after 2s, 3) hard reject after 4s. Degrade action = shorter max_tokens + model fallback + throttle sampling. People?

liam: Need explicit metrics emitted: per-route reject_ratio, degrade_ratio, avg_queue_ms, p95/p99 latency, per-customer token_weight. Also tracing tags to tie degraded requests to outputs for regression evals.

ram: Cost angle: falling back to smaller models cuts token cost ~2.5-3x. Rejects save capacity but are UX-degrading. We should try degrade-first where demo quality is acceptable.

maya: Sounds good. I'll update the RFC with concrete numbers and metric names. Plan: implement in staging A/B (10% degrade mode) for a week, then canary rollout 5% prod -> 25% -> 100% if no regressions. :rocket:

callie: Added a comment on the RFC re: cold-KV-cache scenarios — if cache warmup is the reason for latency, degrade might make things worse. Suggest prefer short queueing in that case until KV-cache warms.

maya: Good catch. We'll add an explicit check: if model cache hit_rate < 50% for worker, prefer short queueing + prioritize warmup requests over degrading sampling params.

liam: SGTM — I'll add infra-tests that simulate cache-cold bursts and validate degrade vs queue behavior.

maya: Thanks all. I'll incorporate feedback and ping again when RFC updated. tagging @oncall for situational awareness. :thumbsup:
